notes: The page continues a correspondence construction: Z induces a map of first direct-image sheaves and then a map on H^1 of the base. A stated compatibility identifies u(x) as the image of u(x′), and the underlined passage asserts its vanishing if the correspondence map vanishes.

The source says “ou ce qui revient au même” about the map on geometric fibres at barred s. This single-fibre equivalence was not proved in this page-local pass: the needed hypotheses on the base and the relevant sheaves are not fully supplied on this page.

Section 2 introduces i:Y→X between proper smooth schemes over an algebraically closed field, with the coefficients in (***) changed from Z to Q. Hypothesis a) requests an algebraic reverse homomorphism whose restriction to Im i* is a right inverse.

The parenthetic NB calls the hypothesis a special case of the “conjectures standart” and says “donc est sans doute touhours vérifiée”. Both the uncertainty qualification and the source spellings are preserved; no conjecture or existence assertion was independently proved.

The final example refers to a hyperplane section and an algebraic Lambda operation, then to lifting to characteristic zero with the polarization. These claims were read, not imported from literature or verified beyond the two local check events.

C/H agreement was not treated as evidence: all ordinary lines, capitals, degrees, subscripts, parentheses, punctuation and source layers were visually compared. The initial ou/oa ambiguity, old d under the r of opération, and post-propriété curved mark arose from that full examination.

The chi-shaped character recurs both as coefficient subscript and after c. It is marked only at its first occurrence; subsequent chi usages do not imply that its intended mathematical value has been settled.

No substantive difference row is assigned merely because H omits a handwritten wrapper. Explicit H provenance claims for propres and both Q letters are evaluated because they disagree with the visible source layers.
H’s explanatory note identifying g as the structural map is editorial matter, not handwriting on this sheet. It is not copied into the diplomatic text or counted as a source omission.

The source has five displays and no diagram or drawing. New-section spacing precedes 2. Soit, and a) has a visible paragraph indent. Other physical line breaks inside the continuous prose are not converted into paragraphs.

The pale curve near propriété attaches the interlinear word to the cancelled ce. Its placement is represented by the inserted macro. The darker terminal curved mark is retained separately as a doubtful comma; no extra authorial drawing is invented.

check_events.outcome: Conditional local check only: assume the displayed objects are sheaves for which H^1(S,-) is the usual additive cohomology functor, and accept the stated compatibility identifying u(x) as the image of u(x′). The zero sheaf homomorphism induces the zero H^1 homomorphism, so that image is zero. This checks the paragraph’s implication from (*)=0, not the construction of the correspondence, its compatibility, or the equivalence with one fibre.

Typed-domain check: write A=H^(2n−1)(X,Q_sub(n)), B=H^(2n−1)(Y,Q_sub(n)), F=i*:A→B, and V:B→A for the reverse map. On Im F, the phrase inverse à droite can mean F∘(V|Im F)=id_Im F; both sides have domain and codomain Im F. Thus the source orientation is coherent and is retained. This does not establish the existence or algebraicity of V.

brief_feedback: Useful clarification: distinguish transcription of literal x-out cells from recoverable underlying letters, and specify a convention for an unreadable predecessor under a probable two-letter overprint. The present pass does not invent the old word under ou. A curved insertion-marker termination that may also be punctuation requires an explicit in-place doubt; this is supplied after propriété.
